title: Synthetic-mix adaptive batch regression sentinel for continuous-batching & queue dynamics
creator: Priya Nair
description: Goal: Build a reproducible load harness and automated detector (the 'sentinel') that surfaces regressions caused by interactions between continuous batching and queueing under mixed tenant/session profiles. Unlike prior probes which focused on single-profile stress or static arrival patterns, this ticket targets correlated multi-profile mixes with stateful KV/prefix continuity and bursty session coupling to expose emergent p95 amplification and tokens/sec regression patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can synthesize at least 6 distinct arrival profiles (short chat, long generation, streaming small tokens, embedding bursts, reranker RPCs, background evals) and compose them into named mixes (e.g., 'consumer+, enterprise-long-tail')
End-to-end run produces Prometheus-compatible metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, queue-depth histogram, batch-size distribution, KV-hit ratio, and model-variant fallback count

Regression sentinel automatically ingests metric windows and raises a signal when p95 increases by >20% relative to baseline AND tokens/sec drops by >10% while batch-size distribution shows increased microbatching (>15% of batches <= 8 tokens)
Dashboard with heatmap + time-series and a weekly synthetic-run report autogenerated and linked to the ticket
Benchmark harness reproducible via docker-compose or k8s job, and a reference GitHub PR with the runner + example YAML mixes
test_plan: Design mix templates: define 6 profiles with inter-arrival distributions (Poisson, Pareto heavy-tail, bursty Poisson), session persistence settings (KV prefix reuse probability), and token length distributions
Implement arrival synthesizer in Go using simulated token streaming. Expose runtime knobs: concurrency, mean inter-arrival, burst intensity, session stickiness, and cold-start fraction
Run baseline sweeps across 3 model variants (float16, int8-quant, cpu-fallback) and 2 routing policies (latency-first, cost-first) to capture baseline surfaces
Collect metrics via Prometheus exporter and export raw traces for offline p95/p99 bootstrapping and KS/ADWIN based drift experiments

Deploy sentinel job that computes rolling windows (5m/30m/2h) and applies combination rules: relative p95 delta, tokens/sec delta, and batch-size shift. Generate alerts to #runtime-bench when triggered
Execute canary: run mix A and mix B daily for 7 days and validate false-positive rate < 5% and detection latency < 30 minutes for injected regressions
implementation_notes: Leverage existing continuous-batching harness components from ENG-4372 and ENG-7420 for kernel-level timing probes but replace arrival generator with stateful session layer
Use FIFO queue simulation with configurable backpressure triggers that emulate the runtime's admission control logic (max inflight, soft-queue-threshold)
Instrument batch-size and queue depth at token emission time rather than request arrival to capture batching effectiveness under different arrival correlations
Regression detection algorithm: combine percent-change rules with distribution-aware tests (two-sample KS for latency distributions + ADWIN for nonstationary drift) to reduce noise sensitivity
Store canonical baselines per-mix & per-release in S3 with metadata (git SHA, model variant, runtime-config) to allow reproducible comparisons
Keep load generator idempotent and seedable so CI can replay failing runs with same seed
dependencies: ENG-61200 (prometheus-exporter-consumer): exporter improvements to include batch-size histogram
ENG-85921 (kv-prefix-sim-api): small API to model KV prefix reuse in test harness
ENG-97812 (routing-policy-sim): read-only config for simulating routing fallback behavior
